content: 1. Veltkamp C, Tonkonogy SL, De Jong YP, Albright C, Grenther WB, Balish E, Terhorst C, and Sartor RB (2001) demonstrated that continuous stimulation by normal luminal bacteria is critical for both the development and maintenance of colitis in Tg(epsilon26) mice. This study was published in Gastroenterology, Volume 120, Issue 4, Pages 900-913. PMID: 11231944. 2. Ley RE, Turnbaugh PJ, Klein S, and Gordon JI (2006) explored the microbial ecology of human gut microbes and their association with obesity. Their findings were published in Nature, Volume 444, Issue 7122, Pages 1022-1023. PMID: 17183309. 3. Turnbaugh PJ, Ley RE, Mahowald MA, Magrini V, Mardis ER, and Gordon JI (2006) identified an obesity-associated gut microbiome with an enhanced capacity for energy harvest. This research was published in Nature, Volume 444, Issue 7122, Pages 1027-1031. PMID: 17183312. 4. Bäckhed F, Manchester JK, Semenkovich CF, and Gordon JI (2007) investigated the mechanisms underlying resistance to diet-induced obesity in germ-free mice. Their study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA, Volume 104, Issue 3, Pages 979-984. PMID: 17210919. 5. Bäckhed F, Ding H, Wang T, Hooper LV, Koh GY, Nagy A, Semenkovich CF, and Gordon JI (2004) examined the role of gut microbiota as an environmental factor that regulates fat storage. This work was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA, Volume 101, Issue 44, Pages 15718-15723. PMID: 15505215.
